core.title: Keep each function at or below 50 code lines
core.given: A function in a non-test production source file inside the scan scope
core.when: its body is written, changed, or scanned
core.then: The function has at most 50 code lines (blank and comment lines excluded).
prefer: Diagnose first: the distinct responsibilities, stages, or invariants the function manages.
Find semantic seams (internal_seam): blocks nameable by one intention-revealing name, often introduced by a comment that becomes the helper's name.
Identify the data each candidate responsibility needs.
Extract one cohesive responsibility at a time.
Name helpers after their purpose, not their mechanics.
Keep related state and decisions together.
Leave the original as a readable top-level flow.
avoid: Splitting at an arbitrary line boundary, or moving contiguous lines elsewhere, just to get under 50.
Mechanical helper names that expose extraction mechanics rather than the responsibility they serve.
Moving a long or complex block unchanged into another function.
A generalized abstraction unrelated to the extracted responsibility.
core.why: A function longer than a screen cannot be read as one unit, so its invariants are reconstructed from memory each time; length catches linear functions doing several unnamed things that complexity misses. The threshold is a sensor for weak cohesion or multiple responsibilities, not the objective — moving lines only removes the signal.
evidence: The length check no longer reports the length finding for the triggering function.
Extracted functions satisfy the applicable complexity and nesting conventions.

Reviewer judges that resulting names and boundaries make the responsibilities easier to understand (a successful refactor identifies a responsibility or cohesive operation that deserves its own name and boundary).
The refactor introduces no new violations of the stack's convention checks.
The refactor keeps existing behavior and existing tests green.
verification: Threshold: a function fails when its code-line count is greater than 50 (at most 50 allowed); the check applies to every production function in scope, newly written or pre-existing, not only changed ones.
code_line: a line inside the function body that is neither blank nor a comment; blank lines and comment lines are not counted.

The check counts non-blank, non-comment lines between the function's signature and the end of its body; body boundaries are found by a matcher that is aware of string and comment literals, so a body delimiter inside a string never closes a body early (a counting invariant only; it does not suppress real findings).

Scope: non-test production source files of the stack's source languages. Unit-test and acceptance-test files are excluded by the rule's own scope, and the stack's never-scanned vendored/generated trees (roots.excluded) are outside the scan. The exact classification of test files and excluded trees is owned by the stack's checker, not by this rule.

Length is the crudest of the per-function metrics and the hardest to argue with; it catches a different fault from the complexity check (a linear function of many sequential assignments may score minimal cyclomatic complexity yet do several things that wanted names).

Severity 2; disposition strict — every finding fails the check run; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline. The rule shares the stack-wide refactor policy that a refactor must keep existing behavior and tests green.

fires: Any non-test production function in the scan scope whose body has more than 50 non-blank, non-comment code lines, whether newly written or pre-existing.
The length check reports the per-function length finding for a function.
A perfectly linear function (cyclomatic complexity 1) of more than 50 sequential code lines.
doesNotFire: A function whose body exceeds 50 physical lines only because of blank lines and comment lines, with at most 50 code lines.
A function with exactly 50 code lines.
Functions in unit-test or acceptance-test files.
Functions in the stack's excluded vendored or build-output trees.

neutralityNotes: The 50-code-line threshold, the code-line definition (non-blank, non-comment), the counting invariant and the severity-2 strict disposition are the rule's own obligation and stay in the core, not the profile. The shared refactor policy (behavior preserved, tests green) is retained in core:evidence[4] and core:verification. The body-extent matcher is stated generically ('a matcher aware of string and comment literals'); the brace-specific wording is the Bun realization. Language (typescript), file kinds (ts/tsx) and the scan glob are realized through profile keys (tooling.languages, suffix.source, roots.scan). roots.excluded is used only as the stack-wide never-scanned vendored/generated tree list ('vendored/build directories'); the test-file exclusion is part of the rule's own scope, and bun.json's deference of the exact exclusion classification to its checker is kept in core:verification rather than the profile. The 'ATDD Bun' runner name is realized by enforcement.runner. Cyclomatic complexity is treated as a language-neutral metric. Detector/validator/finding ids of this rule are bunOnly. The core instantiated with the Bun profile plus the bunOnly items imposes exactly the bun.json obligation: no exception dropped (blank/comment lines uncounted; exactly 50 passes; test and vendored/build trees out of scope) and no obligation added (the shared behavior/test-preservation policy is carried, not strengthened).
